title: Model routing: which tool runs which model, and how a request is resolved
summary: Four blocks that are not text to annotate: a lookup grid, a resolver walk, a precedence ladder and a phased plan. Example data for a routing design review.

blocks.title: Why
blocks.text: Three harnesses can run a review, and each supports a different set of model families. Today the allowed combinations live in prose and the resolver's order lives in code. This page shows both as data, walks one request through the resolver, and lays out the rollout.

rows.label: codex
rows.detail: OpenAI's CLI agent. Runs its own models only.

rows.label: claude
rows.detail: Claude Code. Runs the Claude families and nothing else.

rows.label: opencode
rows.detail: Provider-neutral; any family with an API key, including the corporate gateway.

rows.label: pi
rows.detail: Provider-neutral, but the corporate gateway is untested.

cells.note: works, but pi's gpt adapter has no streaming

cells.hint: run the smoke test before relying on it

blocks.title: One request through the resolver
blocks.input: profile=reviewer, change authored by claude, codex cooling down after a 429

steps.label: --model flag
steps.detail: A flag wins outright and is never validated against the matrix; that is the first question below.

steps.label: Routing rule: reviewer profile
steps.reason: The rule names codex/gpt, but the change was authored by claude, and a reviewer must differ from the author's family.
steps.detail: The author check is a rule-level constraint, so it fires here rather than at the end.

steps.label: Fallback 1: codex/gpt
steps.reason: codex returned 429 four minutes ago; the cooling window is ten.
steps.detail: Cooling is per tool, not per model. Every codex candidate is skipped while it lasts.

steps.label: Fallback 2: opencode/gpt
steps.reason: Valid in the matrix, a different family from the author, not cooling.
steps.detail: The walk ends here. The result carries the reason chain so the run log can show why the model differs from the rule's first choice.

rungs.label: --model flag
rungs.detail: Explicit beats everything. Validated against the matrix only if the question below says so.

rungs.label: Routing rule for the profile
rungs.detail: From the project's routing file, matched on profile and tags.

rungs.label: Workflow default
rungs.detail: The workflow that launched the run may name a model.

rungs.label: Default profile
rungs.detail: The profile's own default, usually a cheap family.
